description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of token counts across eight distinct text categories used in the training of large language models for the Sámi language, as referenced in the paper “Towards a More Inclusive AI: Progress and Perspectives in Large Language Model Training for the Sámi Language.” The vertical axis, labeled “Tokens (K),” represents the number of tokens in thousands, ranging from 0 to 10,000 with tick marks at intervals of 2,000. The horizontal axis, labeled “Categories,” lists the following categories in order: Administrative, Religion, Non-fiction, Fiction, Law, an unlabeled gray bar (likely representing a placeholder or missing label), Science, and Blogs. Each bar is colored light blue except for the unlabeled gray bar. The token counts are explicitly labeled above each bar: Administrative has 6,472K tokens, Religion has 652K, Non-fiction has 1,889K, Fiction has 387K, Law has 354K, the unlabeled gray bar has 10,584K (the highest value), Science has 1,626K, and Blogs has 32K (the lowest value). The bars are not sorted by magnitude, and the unlabeled gray bar, despite its high token count, lacks a category label, suggesting it may represent a major but unnamed corpus component such as general web text or news. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of the unlabeled category and the Administrative category, while Blogs contribute minimally to the overall token corpus.
